subject: Phase 100100 — Fact/Belief epistemic_kind and confidence trajectories (staged diff)
verdict_justification: The core behavior is implemented and independently verified: belief objects, append-only history, create-vs-append gating, as-of reads, dual-backend parity, encryption at rest, and the frozen read contract all pass real tests, clippy, fmt, and per-file coverage (all 84 reported files >=90% functions and lines). The gaps are concurrency (create is check-then-insert outside a transaction), an unconfigurable belief admission key whose doc claims the opposite, and thinner-than-claimed durable telemetry; none is data-corrupting on the happy path.

issues.title: Concurrent first observes race: create is check-then-insert outside a transaction
issues.why_it_matters: belief_observe decides create-vs-append with a read (find_belief_by_proposition), then inserts in a separate transaction. Two observes of the same proposition that both read 'missing' both run the create path; the second violates the unique index and returns InvalidArgument instead of appending. The phase failure table expects concurrent observes to serialize as append.
issues.impact: A legitimate second observation is dropped as an error under concurrency on a new belief identity (no data corruption, but lost evidence and a spurious failure).
issues.proposed_fix: Make create-or-append atomic: either INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then append when zero rows inserted, or catch the duplicate-key error and re-run the append branch, inside the store transaction.

issues.title: Belief admission threshold/prior cannot be configured, yet docs claim the key selects an override
issues.why_it_matters: signals.rs documents BELIEF_KEY as selecting both the type prior and theta_admit override, but 'belief' is not in KNOWN_ADMISSION_KEYS and validate_override_map rejects unknown keys. The belief create gate silently uses the global theta and the fallback prior 0.5 with no way to tune it.
issues.impact: Operators cannot tune belief admission as the code comments promise; belief create behavior diverges from the documented policy surface.
issues.proposed_fix: Add 'belief' to KNOWN_ADMISSION_KEYS with a documented default prior, or correct the signals.rs doc and explicitly state belief create uses the global theta/prior.

issues.title: Durable audit rows omit confidence/source_type; no production sink persists BeliefEvent
issues.why_it_matters: AC-100100-08 cites durable audit_events rows as the telemetry evidence, but those rows carry only {created:true}/{appended:true} in detail_json. FR-15 expects events sufficient to reconstruct the operation (including confidence). The rich BeliefEvent (with confidence and admission_score) is only emitted to an in-memory sink, so a real deployment records no confidence in the durable trail.
issues.impact: The audit trail cannot reconstruct the confidence change of a belief observe; FR-15 reconstruction is weaker than the phase evidence claims.
issues.proposed_fix: Write confidence, source_type, and entry_count into audit_events.detail_json (the columns confidence/source_type already exist), and provide a durable BeliefSink adapter or document the in-memory-only limitation.

issues.title: beliefs.updated_at column is never updated on append and goes stale
issues.why_it_matters: create_belief sets beliefs.updated_at to the first entry's as_of; append_confidence only inserts the entry and an audit row, never touching the belief row. get_belief derives updated_at from the last history entry, so the API and the durable column disagree after any append. The phase 'Known limitations' says updated_at is 'derived rather than stored', which misdescribes a column that is stored and stale.
issues.impact: Any raw-SQL or future consumer reading beliefs.updated_at gets an out-of-date value; the documented limitation is inaccurate.
issues.proposed_fix: UPDATE beliefs SET updated_at = entry.as_of in the append transaction, or drop the column and document derive-only reads.

issues.title: AC-100100-01/T100100-07 evidence overstates: no test rejects a fact carrying a confidence trajectory
issues.why_it_matters: The phase maps T100100-07 ('Fact with confidence_history attach -> Rejected') to AC-100100-01 and cites clio-types/src/belief_tests.rs::fact_items_never_carry_a_trajectory. That test builds a fact item with a scalar confidence and asserts validate() passes; it never attempts to attach a trajectory, and MemoryItem has no such field. The requirement is protected structurally, but the cited evidence does not exercise the stated rejection.
issues.impact: The acceptance-criterion evidence overstates test coverage for a negative case; a reviewer trusting the table would believe a rejection path is tested when it is only type-impossible.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-types/src/belief_tests.rs:133-157; crates/clio-types/src/item.rs:224-268 (no confidence_history field); roadmap/phase-100100...md AC-100100-01 row
issues.proposed_fix: Reword AC-100100-01 to cite the type structure as the guarantee, or add a serialization-boundary test that a fact payload carrying confidence_history is rejected.

issues.title: §4.10 belief object omits epistemic_kind in the struct and table
issues.why_it_matters: The normative §4.10 example JSON carries 'epistemic_kind': 'belief'. BeliefObject (and the serialized belief_history response) expose no epistemic_kind field, and the beliefs table has no such column. Only RetrieveHit carries it. Under Option B a belief is implicitly a belief, so this may be intentional, but it is an undocumented divergence from the §4.10 shape and from FR-14's 'stored ... carries epistemic_kind'.
issues.impact: Consumers reading the concrete belief object (not the RetrieveHit) cannot see the epistemic kind field; the divergence from the normative shape is not stated.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-types/src/belief.rs:110-127; crates/clio-belief/src/history.rs:30-44; sql/001_core.sql beliefs table columns
issues.proposed_fix: Document in the header/identity rule that belief objects are implicitly belief and not 'items', or add an epistemic_kind field to the object.

issues.title: Nine new production files omit the AGENTS.md-mandated closing header line
issues.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md requires the exact header structure ending in 'Keep this module focused on <a single responsibility>'. Nine new production files stop at the Boundary paragraph; only clio-belief/src/lib.rs includes it. (Some pre-existing files such as clio-types/src/item.rs also omit it, so the convention is inconsistent.)
issues.impact: Header-structure compliance gap; no functional impact.
issues.proposed_fix: Append the 'Keep this module focused on ...' line to each new file's module doc, matching clio-belief/src/lib.rs.

issues.title: belief_history not-found uses InvalidArgument rather than a not-found code
issues.why_it_matters: An unknown belief/proposition returns ErrorCode::InvalidArgument with a 'not found' message. No dedicated NotFound code exists yet, so this is acknowledged in the phase's Known limitations, but callers cannot distinguish malformed input from a missing belief by code.
issues.impact: Weak error discrimination for the read API; acknowledged, low impact.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a NotFound error code and use it here (or keep InvalidArgument and state the caller contract explicitly).

issues.title: belief reshape can silently drop orphaned belief_confidence_entries
issues.why_it_matters: reshape_beliefs_sqlite/pg guard destructive drops only by counting rows in the stale beliefs table. If beliefs is empty but belief_confidence_entries holds rows (possible when foreign keys were not enforced), the drop of both tables discards those entries without the ConfigCorrupt guard firing.
issues.impact: Silent loss of orphaned history rows during an undeployed-schema reshape; narrow but real.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/belief_reshape.rs:104-123 and :129-148 (count beliefs only); :53-58 / :90-98 drop both tables
issues.proposed_fix: Also count belief_confidence_entries rows (when the table exists) and refuse the drop when either is non-empty.

issues.title: belief_history as_of filtering relies on free-form string ordering
issues.why_it_matters: Entries and the as_of filter are stored/compared as text (e.as_of <= ?3). Mixed date-only ('2026-06-01') and timestamp ('2026-06-01T12:00:00Z') values compare lexicographically, so a same-day timestamp entry can be excluded or misordered relative to a date-only query. The format contract is undocumented.
issues.impact: Point-in-time results are ambiguous when callers mix date-only and timestamp formats; only affects NFR-4 reads at same-day boundaries.
issues.proposed_fix: Document the accepted as_of format and normalize to a single canonical form on write, or compare parsed instants.

findings.title: Concurrent first observes race: create is check-then-insert outside a transaction
findings.recommendation: Make create-or-append atomic (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then append, or retry-on-duplicate into the append branch) within one store transaction.

resolution.fix: Resolved. observe.rs:68-96 added append_to_existing helper; the create branch now retries: on create_belief failure it re-resolves the proposition and appends when the identity exists (the create-race winner), else propagates the original error (observe.rs:316-324). Covered by observe_flow_tests.rs::create_race_loser_appends_instead_of_erroring (deterministic stale-read loser appends), ::create_race_loser_propagates_error_when_identity_is_gone (identity vanished -> original duplicate error), and ::concurrent_first_observes_serialize_as_append (two real threads, one create + one append, history=2, no error). Matches the phase-100100 failure table row 'Concurrent observes -> Serializable append'.

findings.title: Belief admission threshold/prior cannot be configured although docs claim the key selects an override
findings.recommendation: Add 'belief' to KNOWN_ADMISSION_KEYS with a documented default, or correct the doc to state the global theta/prior applies.

resolution.fix: Resolved by making the key configurable (the finding's first option). admission_knobs.rs:48 added 'belief' to KNOWN_ADMISSION_KEYS; default_type_prior('belief') = Some(0.50) (matches the historical fallback, so behavior is unchanged); override-map error message now says 'known category, episodic type, or belief key'. signals.rs BELIEF_KEY doc now states the default prior 0.5 and global-theta fallback. Test: admission_knobs_tests.rs::belief_create_key_is_tunable; knob_defaults_follow_appendix updated to 11 keys.

findings.title: Durable audit rows omit confidence/source_type and no production sink persists BeliefEvent
findings.recommendation: Persist confidence/source_type/entry_count in audit_events.detail_json (or the existing columns) and/or provide a durable BeliefSink.

resolution.fix: Resolved. belief_store.rs:134-152 adds belief_audit_detail(); both backends now write the audit_events.confidence column ($N::float8 on Postgres, matching the postgres_memory.rs item-audit pattern) and detail_json {created|appended, confidence, source_type, entry_count}. Evidence: belief_tests.rs::sqlite_belief_audit_rows_carry_reconstruction_fields and ::postgres_belief_audit_rows_carry_reconstruction_fields assert the confidence column and all detail fields for create (0.4/agent_inferred/1) and append (0.65/agent_inferred/2) on both backends. Durable BeliefSink adapter deliberately not added: audit_events IS the durable ordered trail (indexed by item_id+created_at); a second stream would duplicate it. admission_score is not persisted on the belief create row (documented in the phase Known limitations).

findings.title: beliefs.updated_at column is never updated on append and goes stale
findings.recommendation: Update beliefs.updated_at in the append transaction or drop the column and document derive-only reads.

resolution.fix: Resolved by maintaining the column. append_confidence now runs UPDATE beliefs SET updated_at = (SELECT MAX(as_of) FROM belief_confidence_entries WHERE belief_id=?) inside the append transaction (sqlite_belief.rs:159-166, postgres_belief.rs:158-167); create stores max-by-as_of instead of vector-last so the column always matches the derived read (SQL ORDER BY as_of). Asserted by the new audit-reconstruction tests (updated_at == '2026-07-14' read from the raw column on both backends).

findings.title: AC-100100-01/T100100-07 evidence overstates: no test rejects a fact carrying a confidence trajectory
findings.recommendation: Cite the type structure as the guarantee or add a serialization-boundary negative test.

resolution.fix: Resolved by rewording the evidence (the finding's first option). The phase AC-100100-01 row now states T100100-07's rejection is structural: MemoryItem has no confidence_history field (a fact cannot carry a trajectory by type) and item.validate rejects source_type on facts; fact_items_never_carry_a_trajectory asserts a fact with scalar confidence validates and there is no runtime rejection path to call. No misleading test claim remains.

findings.title: §4.10 belief object omits epistemic_kind in the struct and table
findings.recommendation: Document the Option-B implicit-kind divergence, or add the field.

resolution.fix: Resolved by documenting the Option-B divergence (the finding's first option). clio-types/src/belief.rs BeliefObject doc now states: under Option B a belief object is implicitly epistemic_kind='belief'; beliefs are NOT items and carry no separate kind field/column/parameter; the kind is surfaced explicitly on reads via RetrieveHit. No schema change.

findings.title: Nine new production files omit the AGENTS.md-mandated closing header line
findings.recommendation: Append 'Keep this module focused on ...' to each new file's module doc.

resolution.fix: Resolved. The closing 'Keep this module focused on ...' header line was appended to all nine files: clio-belief/src/{history,observe,signals}.rs, clio-types/src/{belief,read}.rs, clio-store/src/{belief_reshape,belief_store,postgres_belief,sqlite_belief}.rs, matching clio-belief/src/lib.rs.

findings.title: belief_history not-found uses InvalidArgument rather than a not-found code
findings.recommendation: Add a NotFound code or document the caller contract.

resolution.fix: Resolved by adding the code (the finding's first option). clio-types/src/error.rs adds ErrorCode::NotFound ('not_found', stable as_str asserted in error.rs tests); clio-belief/src/history.rs::not_found now returns it; history_tests.rs::unknown_belief_returns_structured_not_found asserts NotFound for both the unknown-target and cross-bank cases. Phase Known limitations updated.

findings.title: belief reshape can silently drop orphaned belief_confidence_entries
findings.recommendation: Count belief_confidence_entries rows too and refuse the drop when either table is non-empty.

resolution.fix: Resolved. belief_reshape.rs now counts belief_confidence_entries rows too (sqlite_entry_rows/pg_entry_rows handle the table-not-exists case) and refuses the destructive drop with a combined ConfigCorrupt message when either table is non-empty. Tests: belief_reshape_tests.rs::orphaned_confidence_entries_are_preserved (sqlite) and the extended ::pg_beliefs_reshape_guard (orphaned entries alone refuse the drop).

findings.title: belief_history as_of filtering relies on free-form string ordering
findings.recommendation: Document/normalize the as_of format or compare parsed instants.

resolution.fix: Resolved by documenting the format contract (the finding's documentation option). clio-types/src/belief.rs ConfidenceEntry::as_of and BeliefObject::as_of_confidence, clio-store/src/belief_store.rs belief_history, and clio-belief/src/history.rs now state: as_of orders and filters as lexicographic ISO-8601 text; use ONE canonical form per trajectory (date-only or full timestamp), never mix. Phase Known limitations states the same. Normalizing stored history entries was rejected: it would rewrite append-only rows (FR-13).

dismissed: decide() losing its category gate: verification shows the whitelist lived in decide_raw via typed Candidate parsing, not in decide; the refactor to decide_ungated is behavior-preserving and all admission tests pass.

ConfidenceEntry/BeliefObject array-order current_confidence vs as_of ordering: stored histories are loaded ORDER BY as_of, so current_* is correct on every read path; only a hand-built out-of-order BeliefObject could differ, and no production caller does that.
Cross-subject evidence mixing on a shared proposition key: identity is (bank_id, proposition_key) by documented design, and subject_id only selects the DEK; bank remains the isolation boundary.
No DB trigger enforcing append-only history: the trait exposes only append/create with no UPDATE/DELETE path, so the API boundary is append-only.
Schema version bump 4->5 with fail-closed ConfigCorrupt on non-empty legacy beliefs: the phase explicitly permits fail-closed for pre-epistemic rows and the tables are undeployed.
roadmap-isolation: no references to roadmap/, phase numbers, or crates.md found in crates/ or sql/.

strengths: Append-only history holds at both the API and SQL layers; prior entries are asserted byte-identical after append on both backends.
Encryption-at-rest and crypto-shredding fail-closed behavior is genuinely tested (ciphertext hides plaintext, destroyed DEK returns Forbidden).
Create/append admission split is implemented as specified: no category gate on create, no re-scoring on append.
The frozen RetrieveHit contract and its golden JSON fixtures make the fact-vs-belief read shape unambiguous for slice 100120.
Claims in the phase file were independently reproducible: tests, clippy, fmt, and per-file coverage all match.
regrets: The review is diff-centered; broader pre-existing assumptions (e.g., item-level epistemic enforcement owned by Phase 100030) were spot-checked rather than exhaustively traced.
No live concurrency probe was run for F-01; the finding rests on code reading plus the documented failure-mode table.
process_changes: Add a concurrent create-or-append test to the belief suite so the race is observable rather than inferred.
Treat 'durable telemetry' claims as requiring inspection of the actual durable row contents, not just the in-memory event struct.
